An X-shaped older capital, the isolated dash, and the dense older comparison material are preserved separately.

Display (6) gives a chain of set-difference expressions for the ring-epsilon Sigma. The round superscript remains circle/o/zero uncertain. The local omega form is resolved from its two rounded turns and direct comparison with (7); the relation after it remains uncertain.

Display (7) presents the three separated pieces named again in the prose “ens. mutuellement disjoints.” The word “trois” is visibly cancelled. Both epsilon entries in its right parenthesis carry a detached high prime; that observation is retained although the preceding parenthesis in (6) has an unprimed first entry. The buried low suffixes remain open.

In (8), each of the first three overbars extends across the Sigma and its ring-epsilon superscript. The final Sigma has a separate high dot and a small comma between its ring and epsilon. The isolated lower terminal mark has connected loop/stem/arm/tail strokes and remains uncertain.

Two separately struck draft lines precede 1.2. Their words read “On a le cas” and “on s’intéresse à la cond”. The latter stops after the visible d and its terminal stroke; no ending or abbreviation point is supplied.

Section 1.2 writes two binary families and names “non parallèles”. Only parallèles is underlined. The full group “si elles sont distinctes, et” is interlinear, with its bent leader attaching before “s’il existe”. H’s explicit note already identifies this group as interlinear, so its absence of an add macro was not counted as a separate difference.

Display (10) is the intersection with a slashed empty-set oval. The two following displays write the two inclusions with exchanged indices and signs. Their introducing prose ends in written colons: “condition qui équivaut :” and “ou encore :”. The final displayed definitions are copied with the reduced last indices still uncertain.

Direct shape comparisons used during reading were: the two omega forms on this page; distinct high prime strokes versus low overwritten suffixes in (7); the first low upright 1 versus the hooked second index in the final prose; and the live epsilon shapes beside the old small corrected forms. The surrounding formula patterns were noted but did not settle the damaged suffixes or the final label.

The two-legged family glyph is marked pi/Pi uncertain at its first occurrence. Its repeated cap and descending legs are copied consistently afterwards. The last tag has a 7-like cap and downward stroke, with 2 retained as an alternative; the numerical order of the preceding tags does not decide the ink.
